tasks.title: Singleton DB connection
tasks.issue: getDb() calls new Database(DB_PATH) on every request and re-runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS every time. Wastes file handles and prevents WAL optimisations.
tasks.fix: Add module-level singleton and enable WAL on first open: let _db; function getDb() { if (!_db) { _db = new Database(DB_PATH); _db.pragma('journal_mode = WAL'); _db.exec('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes ...'); } return _db; }
acceptance_criteria: getDb() returns same instance on repeated calls
WAL pragma is set exactly once
All existing tests still pass

tasks.title: Paginate GET /api/notes
tasks.issue: SELECT * FROM notes ORDER BY id DESC returns every row with no LIMIT. Full table scan on every history load.
tasks.fix: Add LIMIT/OFFSET with optional ?page= query param. Default page size 50. const page = Math.max(0, parseInt(req.query.page) || 0); const PAGE_SIZE = 50; db.prepare('SELECT * FROM notes ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?').all(PAGE_SIZE, page * PAGE_SIZE);
acceptance_criteria: GET returns max 50 rows by default
GET ?page=1 returns next 50
Response includes a total count field

tasks.title: Enforce raw_text size limit
tasks.issue: No upper bound on raw_text length. A huge payload blocks the Node.js event loop inside parseNote().
tasks.fix: Reject before parsing: if (rawText.length > 50000) { return res.status(413).json({ error: 'Note exceeds 50000 character limit.' }); }
acceptance_criteria: POST with more than 50000 chars returns 413
POST with exactly 50000 chars returns 201
Error body is { error: string }

tasks.title: Validate Content-Type on POST
tasks.issue: Missing Content-Type causes Next.js to skip JSON body parsing. req.body becomes undefined and the error message is misleading.
tasks.fix: Check header early: if (req.method === 'POST' && !req.headers['content-type']?.includes('application/json')) { return res.status(415).json({ error: 'Content-Type must be application/json' }); }
acceptance_criteria: POST without Content-Type: application/json returns 415
POST with correct header still works

tasks.title: Add HTTP security headers
tasks.issue: No security headers set. Needed before any deployment.
tasks.fix: Add async headers() to next.config.js returning X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin for source '/(.*)'.
acceptance_criteria: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff present on all responses
X-Frame-Options: DENY present on all responses

tasks.title: Extract repository layer from API route
tasks.issue: The handler does HTTP parsing, calls parseNote(), executes SQL, and shapes the response — 4 responsibilities in one function.
tasks.fix: Create lib/notesRepository.js with createNote(rawText) and listNotes(page). The API route becomes a thin adapter that only handles HTTP.
acceptance_criteria: lib/notesRepository.js exists with createNote() and listNotes()
pages/api/notes.js contains no SQL
api.test.js tests the repository directly

tasks.title: Fix CommonJS and ESM mix
tasks.issue: notes.js uses export default (ESM) but db/init.js and lib/parser.js use require() (CommonJS). This caused Jest to require inlining the handler.
tasks.fix: Pick one module system and apply consistently across all files. Recommended: convert db/init.js and lib/parser.js to ESM with export function.
acceptance_criteria: All files use the same module system
api.test.js can import the handler directly

tasks.title: Fix parser false-positive on 'agreed to' and 'we decided'
tasks.issue: lower.includes('we decided') and lower.includes('agreed to') misclassify lines with negations like 'We decided not to do this'.
tasks.fix: Restrict to lines that start with the phrase: /^we decided/.test(lower) || /^agreed to/.test(lower)
acceptance_criteria: 'We decided not to proceed' is NOT classified as a decision
'Decision: Proceed' still IS classified as a decision
Existing parser tests still pass

tasks.title: Add safe JSON.parse fallback in GET handler
tasks.issue: JSON.parse(row.decisions_json) throws on malformed data, crashing the entire GET response.
tasks.fix: Add helper: function safeParseArray(str) { try { return JSON.parse(str); } catch { return []; } } and use it for all three JSON fields.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/notes does not 500 when one row has malformed JSON
The malformed row returns empty arrays for affected fields
